Landslides Disrupt Hospitality Properties in Western Norway

A series of landslides triggered by persistent rainfall has severely affected hospitality sites in Norway’s Vestland region, with ongoing disruptions to hotels, conference centers, and mountain lodges. The event, which began late last week and shows no sign of abating, has forced several properties to evacuate guests and staff, and left others inaccessible due to blocked access routes operated by the businesses themselves.

According to the Norwegian Hospitality Association, at least nine major sites operated by member firms have reported significant damage. “We are seeing extensive mud and water intrusion into ground-floor facilities, including kitchens and guest areas,” said Association spokesperson Lise Fagerheim. “Staff safety remains our top priority, and several locations have temporarily closed while we assess structural impacts.”

Sognefjord Resorts, a leading local operator, reported that one of its mountain lodges sustained structural damage to its dining hall and guest rooms. “Our team acted quickly to move all guests and employees to safety, but the situation remains challenging as further slides are possible,” said operations manager Eirik Halvorsen.

Industry analysts estimate that over 200 hospitality workers in the region have been displaced from their workplaces, either due to site closures or ongoing evacuation orders. “The operational disruption is significant, especially for properties relying on summer bookings,” noted analyst Martine Oppedal.

The Norwegian Hospitality Association is coordinating with local authorities to monitor the evolving situation. “Our focus is on ensuring the wellbeing of workers and guests, and on supporting member firms through these unprecedented challenges,” Fagerheim added. Firms continue to assess damages as the landslide threat persists.
